बॉलीवुड से आई एक बेहद दुखद खबर ने फैंस और स्टार्स को हिलाकर रख दिया है! 💔

59 साल के मशहूर डायरेक्टर Sanjay Gupta का शनिवार को अपने मुंबई वाले घर पर अचानक निधन हो गया। वर्सोवा पुलिस की रिपोर्ट के मुताबिक CCTV फुटेज में दिखा कि रात लगभग 2 बजे ड्राइंग रूम से किचन जाते वक्त उनका बैलेंस बिगड़ा और वे दीवार से टकराकर गिर गए, जिसके बाद पुलिस ने ADR दर्ज किया है। 🎥

इस दर्दनाक हादसे से एक्टर Hrithik Roshan का दिल पूरी तरह से टूट गया है और उन्होंने अपने X अकाउंट पर एक बेहद भावुक ट्रिब्यूट शेयर किया है। 🥺

2017 की फिल्म Kaabil में साथ काम कर चुके Hrithik ने लिखा कि उनके साथ सिर्फ एक फिल्म काफी नहीं थी और वे इस सबसे बेहतरीन एक्सपीरियंस के लिए हमेशा उनके शुक्रगुजार रहेंगे। 🎬

1994 की फिल्म Aatish: Feel the Fire से करियर शुरू करने वाले Sanjay Gupta ने Kaante और Zinda जैसी फिल्में बनाईं, वहीं 208 करोड़ रुपये कमाने वाली Kaabil उनकी सबसे बड़ी हिट साबित हुई थी।

Sanjay Gupta की बनाई फिल्मों में से आपकी सबसे पसंदीदा फिल्म कौन सी है? कमेंट्स में जरूर बताएं!

ctx.title: Heartbroken Hrithik Roshan remembers director Sanjay Gupta in moving tribute, thanks him for the best experience during the making of Kaabil
ctx.summary: Hrithik Roshan worked with Sanjay Gupta in Kaabil. The director died after falling and hitting his head at his home on Saturday.
ctx.text:
The Hindi film industry is mourning with the sudden demise of director Sanjay Gupta on Saturday. The filmmaker died at his residence after he slipped and hit his head. He was 59. Actor Hrithik Roshan has now penned a moving tribute to the director, with whom he worked in the 2017 film Kaabil.
Hrithik shared a picture with Sanjay in his X account and wrote in the caption, “Sanjay , I'm gonna miss you man. One film with you wasn't enough ... I will always remember our time together with so much love for you .. your laughter, your passion , that child in you that lit up with every good idea , there was so much more we needed to do together man , this is way too soon.”
He added, "I am gonna remember you with so much gratitude my friend , I wish I had hugged you harder and thanked you for giving me the best experience of my life with kaabil. Nobody will fully know how much you gave that film. I'm heartbroken , this was too soon.
The Versova police have registered an accidental death report (ADR) in connection with the incident and are probing to ascertain the exact sequence of events. The police were informed in the morning about the death of Sanjay Gupta.
The police said the CCTV footage of the house shows that around 2.00 am. Gupta, who was sitting in the drawing room, went to the kitchen and later lost his balance and fell against the wall.
Born in 1967 in Mumbai, Sanjay Gupta began his career at age 26 with the 1994 release, Aatish: Feel the Fire, starring Sanjay Dutt, Aditya Pancholi, Raveena Tandon, Karisma Kapoor and Atul Agnihotri.
Over the next few years, he developed expertise in making gangster films, culminating in the 2002 film Kaante, starring Amitabh Bachchan, Sanjay Dutt,. Suniel Shetty, Kumar Gaurav, Lucky Ali, and Mahesh Manjrekar. Widely regarded as his best work and one of the best gangster films to come out of Bollywood, it was inspired by Quentin Tarantino's Reservoir Dogs. He followed this up with critically acclaimed and successful films such as Zinda, starring Sanjay Dutt and John Abraham. One of his most high-profile films was the Hrithik Roshan-starrer Kaabil, which earned ₹ 208 crore worldwide, emerging as his highest-grosser.
Santanu Das is a Senior Content Producer at Hindustan Times with over 5 years of experience, writing on films, pop culture and film festivals. He has a keen interest in writing about South Asian independent films and has covered several film festivals, including Sundance and CPH: Docx. He also brings a sharp perspective to the monthly column called The Fault in Our Stars, where he writes about a recent film/series and what stops the ‘good’ from becoming ‘great’.

A gold medalist from Banaras Hindu University, Santanu completed his postgraduate studies in English from Jadavpur University. He is also a Rotten Tomatoes-certified film critic. When not watching films or speaking to celebrities, Santanu can be found reading a book. Some of his favourite films are Aparajito, Ponyo and The Double Life of Veronique. His favourite books include The Corrections, The God of Small Things and A Room of One's Own.

Santanu continues to write passionately about films and celebrity culture. He brings a relatable, as well as critically informed, lens to entertainment and culture for a wide audience.
